To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a slow pressor ANG II infusion for 2 wk increased O₂⁻ production in the MD by 3.8-fold, primarily by enhancing expression and activity of both Nox2 and 4.
a subpressor ANG II dose increases Nox2 and -4 expression and activity in the MD and increases O₂⁻ production in the MD.
chronic ANG II infusion enhances MD-derived O₂−, and the sources of this enhanced O₂− are primarily Nox4 and Nox2.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of Nox-derived superoxide in the pathophysiology of hypertension and kidney disease.
the role of the macula densas (MD) in the development of hypertension.
the role of Nox2, Nox4, and p22(phox), which is a subunit of both, in ANG II-stimulation of MD O₂⁻ production and its role in the development of hypertension.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ANG II-induced increase in Nox activity in the MD may contribute to the increased renal tubular sodium reabsorption and increased renal vascular tone in ANG II-dependent hypertension.
chronic elevations in circulating levels of ANG II enhance O₂⁻ release by the MD through increased expression of Nox2, Nox4, and p22(phox).
ANG II enhances MD-derived O₂- generation in a subpressor dose-dependent manner and that the source of this O₂- is primarily Nox2, with a minor contribution by Nox4.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ANG II-induced chronic hypertension enhances O₂⁺ production in MD cells, and this is mediated primarily through Nox2 and partially through Nox4.
chronic ANG II elevations increase O₂⁻ production by the MD through upregulation of Nox2/Nox4 and that this increase in O₂⁻ may contribute to the progression of hypertension.
chronic elevations in circulating ANG II during hypertension increases MD-derived O₂− primarily through Nox2 and/or Nox4, which may contribute to hypertension.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MD is an important source of superoxide in the kidney during ANG II-mediated hypertension and that this superoxide is derived from Nox2 and/or Nox4.
chronic elevations in circulating ANG II enhance O₂⁻ production by the MD and this is mediated by Nox2 and/or Nox4.
ANG II-induced increases in MD-derived O₂− are mediated by Nox2 and/or Nox4 and are not mediated by NADPH oxidases other than Nox2 and/ or Nox4.
